svg.title: Making time for a shared activity

text.tspan: Making time for a shared activity
When we spend time with someone who cares for us, a little care can make the experience
better. Planning and thinking about other people both help.
First, a simple shared activity creates space for conversation. For example, we choose a short
walk that suits everyone’s pace. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, attention matters more than an elaborate plan. For example, we put our phones away
and ask about a familiar memory. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can spend time with someone who cares for us more easily when we prepare and notice
other people. These simple steps give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Tell a friend about a time you tried to spend time with someone who cares for us. What did you do? What would you change?
Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: say what you
want to do; explain the first step; explain a different second step; say why the two steps help.)
